rationale: PINS THE EXCLUSION that must not widen when `require(...)` becomes a recognized signal. The fix accepts a `call_expression` whose callee is the bare `require` identifier or the `import` keyword, so that a CommonJS `require("child_process")` sets the child_process signal. A `member_expression` callee is somebody else's method: `loader.require("child_process")` is a custom call, not the module loader, and must NOT arm the rule — otherwise every project with a `require` method on any object would get its own bare `exec` reported as Node's shell. This needs its own fixture because the signals are per-FILE: in a file that also contained one real `require("child_process")` the signal would be set regardless, and the negative would be unobservable.

expectTaintSinks.note: The signal never arrives: nothing in this file imports child_process. `loader.require("child_process")` is a member call and is deliberately NOT counted, so the project's own `exec` must stay unreported — the rule must not degrade back into 'any bare exec is a shell'.
